## Answer

**AV3-007 (Aeris V3, CHC, firmware 1.9.2)** had the worst unplanned downtime rate among the 254 devices under 500 operating hours: **68 minutes over 76 hours ≈ 89.5 min per 100 operating hours**.

**How I got there** (downtime-per-hour isn't a rankable field, so I bounded it):

| Device | Model | Hours | Downtime | Min/100h |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AV3-007** | Aeris V3 | 76 | 68 | **89.5** |
| IL7-032 | InfusaLine 700 | 453 | 314 | 69.3 |
| IL4-147 | InfusaLine 400 | 132 | 82 | 62.1 |
| IL4-084 | InfusaLine 400 | 206 | 127 | 61.7 |
| IL4-026 | InfusaLine 400 | 167 | 90 | 53.9 |
| IL4-033 | InfusaLine 400 | 149 | 64 | 43.0 |

The ranking is complete rather than a spot check: no unexamined device can beat 89.5 min/100h. Among the 200–500 hour devices, a rate that high would require >179 downtime minutes, and only IL7-032 (314) exceeds that — everything else in the band tops out at 127. In the 100–200 hour band, it would require >89.5 minutes, and the band maximum is IL4-026 at 90 (which yields only 53.9). Below 100 hours there are just 20 devices, and after AV3-007 the next-highest downtime is 24 minutes (AV3-014, 98 h → 24.5).

**Risk-score comparison:** AV3-007 carries a vendor risk score of **57**, well below the highest-scored Aeris V3 in the fleet, **AV3-024 at 85** (616 h, firmware 2.0.0). Notably, AV3-024 — the unit the vendor flagged as most at risk — logged only 67 downtime minutes across 616 hours, about **10.9 min per 100 hours**, roughly one-eighth of AV3-007's rate. The vendor's advance risk scoring is tracking something other than realised downtime here; AV3-007 is a young, low-hour unit on older firmware (1.9.2 vs 2.0.0) that is failing far more per hour of use than its moderate score suggests.

FINAL: AV3-007 vs AV3-024

## Answer

**AV3-007 (Aeris V3, site CHC)** had the most unplanned downtime per operating hour among devices under 500 hours: **68 min over 76 hours = 89.5 min per 100 operating hours**.

**How I found it.** Downtime *per hour* isn't a rankable field, so raw downtime leaders are misleading — IL7-032 tops the list with 314 minutes but has 453 hours, diluting its rate to 69.3. I split the 254 low-hour devices into hour bands and ranked downtime within each. Since every device in a band has at least the band's lower bound of hours, the band leader's downtime divided by that bound caps the rate for the whole band, which let me rule out most bands without inspecting them:

| Band (hrs) | Leader | Max possible rate /100h |
|---|---|---|
| <50 | AV3-030 (5 min) | 14.3 actual (all 3 checked) |
| 50–100 | AV3-007 (68 min) | **89.5 actual** |
| 100–150 | IL4-147 (82 min) | ≤82 (62.1 actual) |
| 150–200 | IL4-026 (90 min) | ≤60 |
| 200–300 | IL4-084 (127 min) | ≤63.5 |
| 300–500 | IL7-032 (314 min) | ≤104.7 (69.3 actual) |

Only the <50, 50–100 and 300–500 bands could beat 82, and checking their actual hours settled it. Runners-up inside AV3-007's own band cap out at 48/100h, so it wins outright.

**Risk score comparison.** AV3-007 carries a vendor risk score of **57**, well below the highest-risk Aeris V3, **AV3-024 at 85** — a 28-point gap, and AV3-007 doesn't even reach the model's top three (85, 81, 79). The vendor's advance risk scoring did not flag the Aeris V3 unit that actually accrued the worst downtime rate in the low-hour fleet, which is worth raising with the vendor.

## Answer

**Device with the highest unplanned downtime per operating hour (under 500 h): AV3-007 (Aeris V3, site CHC, firmware 1.9.2)**

How I got there: downtime-per-hour isn't a rankable field, so I ranked raw `downtime_min` within the sub-500-hour population (254 devices) and then within progressively tighter hour bands (<250, <160, <100, <40), pulling full records to compute the ratio — this bounds the search, since a device can only win by having either large downtime or very few hours.

| Device | Model | Hours | Downtime (min) | Per 100 h | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AV3-007** | Aeris V3 | 76 | 68 | **89.5** | 57 |
| IL7-032 | InfusaLine 700 | 453 | 314 | 69.3 | 99 |
| IL4-147 | InfusaLine 400 | 132 | 82 | 62.1 | 70 |
| IL4-084 | InfusaLine 400 | 206 | 127 | 61.7 | 99 |
| IL4-026 | InfusaLine 400 | 167 | 90 | 53.9 | 43 |

No other device can displace AV3-007: the largest downtime below 250 h is 127 min (IL4-084, 206 h), and in the 250–500 h band a device would need >224 min of downtime, which only IL7-032 approaches (314 min, but at 453 h). The very-low-hour devices (<40 h) have near-zero downtime.

**Risk comparison:** AV3-007 carries a vendor risk score of only **57**, well below the highest-risk Aeris V3 in the fleet, **AV3-024 at 85** (which is unremarkable on downtime). So the vendor's advance risk scoring did not flag the unit that is actually losing the most service time per hour of use — worth checking whether the 1.9.2 firmware on AV3-007 is a factor, as its downtime is roughly 3.5× that of the next-worst Aeris V3.

FINAL: AV3-007 vs AV3-024
